resources.name: Tele-Law
resources.runBy: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, through Common Service Centres
resources.summary: Legal advice before any case is filed, given by a panel lawyer over video call or telephone. Tele-Law's own FAQ says the service is free of cost for all citizens, that it is available through Common Service Centres (CSCs) at gram panchayat level across the States and Union Territories, and that a Tele-Law mobile app connects a person to a panel lawyer directly.
resources.whoItIsFor: Anyone, according to Tele-Law's FAQ, which lists matters such as family disputes, domestic violence, sexual harassment at the workplace, maintenance, property and land, equal wages, maternity benefits, child protection and registering an FIR. A para-legal volunteer or the CSC operator registers the request and books the call.

contacts.label: Find a Common Service Centre and para-legal volunteer in your State

resources.name: NALSA: free legal aid through the Legal Services Authorities
resources.runBy: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, with the State, District and Taluk Legal Services Authorities and Committees
resources.summary: Free legal services in civil and criminal matters for the categories named in Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987: advice, a lawyer to conduct a case, court fees and paperwork, and Lok Adalats for settling disputes. NALSA's legal-aid page says a person can apply at the front office of the nearest Legal Services Authority, which sits in the court premises, by post, by email, online, or orally with the help of a para-legal volunteer.
resources.whoItIsFor: Section 12 covers, among others, women and children, members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities, industrial workmen, persons in custody, victims of trafficking, mass disasters or violence, and persons whose annual income is below the ceiling set for their State (the State-wise limits are listed on NALSA's legal-aid page). NALSA's FAQ adds that a person outside these categories can still approach a Legal Services Institution for legal advice and assistance. The Authority decides each application.

resources.name: National Consumer Helpline (1915)
resources.runBy: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
resources.summary: A helpline and online portal for registering a grievance about goods that were bought or a service that was paid for, and for tracking what happens to it. Grievances can be registered by phone, on the portal, by SMS or WhatsApp, and through the NCH and UMANG apps.
resources.whoItIsFor: Consumers with a complaint against a seller or a service provider. Whether a particular complaint is one the helpline takes up is for the helpline to say.
resources.hours: Helpline: every day except national holidays, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM

contacts.label: Register or track a grievance online

resources.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and helpline 1930
resources.runBy: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
resources.summary: For reporting cyber crime, including money lost to online financial fraud. The portal's page of State nodal officers states that online financial fraud is reported on the national cyber crime helpline 1930. The portal itself takes complaints online under three heads: crime against women or children, financial fraud, and other cyber crime.

contacts.label: National cyber crime helpline, for online financial fraud

resources.name: Emergency number 112
resources.runBy: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), Ministry of Home Affairs, answered by each State's and Union Territory's emergency response centre
resources.summary: India's single emergency number. The Ministry of Home Affairs describes ERSS-112 as one number for every kind of emergency: the call is taken at the State's answering point and passed, with its details, to the police, health, fire, disaster, women's or children's service that needs to respond.

resources.name: Women Helpline 181
resources.runBy: Ministry of Women and Child Development, run by the States and Union Territories
resources.summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development lists 181 as the toll-free Women Helpline: the number for a woman who needs help or information.

resources.name: Child Helpline 1098
resources.runBy: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development lists 1098 as the toll-free Child Helpline: the number for a child who needs help, and for anyone who is worried about a child.

resources.name: SHe-Box: sexual harassment at the workplace
resources.runBy: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development's website links SHe-Box as the place to register a complaint of sexual harassment at the workplace.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS mental health helpline (14416)
resources.runBy: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Tele Mental Health Programme
resources.summary: A toll-free tele-mental-health service of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Its website says a call to either number connects the caller with a counsellor.
